issues.body: `_collect_defuse_prs` catches each arbitrary exception, prints an ALERT, and returns no indication that collection deferred; `_execute_defuse_actions` likewise catches mutation-boundary revalidation failures before incrementing `attempted` and neither appends `deferred` nor increments a completed count. If every admissible PR fails at either boundary, the resulting defuse `PhaseOutcome` is `(changed=0, attempted=0, deferred=())`, so `phase_exit_failure` returns `None`. That violates the module's precedence rule that an all-object failure is systemic and makes the newly broadened catch convert a repeated malformed-payload/runtime failure into a green run. The new collection and revalidation tests deliberately include a succeeding #31/#22, so they cannot detect this all-failed path.
issues.fix_hint: Carry collection and pre-attempt revalidation deferrals into the defuse phase outcome (with accounting that lets `phase_exit_failure` distinguish no candidates from candidates that all failed), and add separate all-candidates-fail self-tests for both boundaries asserting a non-zero systemic exit reason. Preserve the existing one-fails/one-completes continuation cases.
issues.title: All defuse read failures are swallowed into an exit-zero sweep

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The widened exception boundaries generally preserve the intended per-object continuation and masking, but the defuse read paths do not preserve the shared systemic-failure precedence. Both collection and mutation-boundary revalidation can now catch arbitrary failures for every candidate while returning an empty/healthy-looking outcome, so the sweep exits zero after doing no defuse work. The added tests cover head-of-line continuation and masking but omit the all-failed case that exposes this vacuity.
